title: Diffusion and generated media
goal: Explain the denoising idea and judge an image with a consistent checklist.
case: A college needs a synthetic poster image while respecting consent and image rights.
terms: In a common training setup, progressively add noise to a clean image.
A learned model estimates how to remove noise at each step; the course simulation uses the known clean target.
Text or other inputs can guide generation. The condition does not guarantee accurate details.
Check whether text, people, permissions and task-specific details meet the brief.
steps: Inspect a 4 by 4 synthetic clean image
Add reproducible noise at two strengths
Use a transparent toy denoising demonstration
Compare two prepared descriptions using one rubric
example: Clean grid has an L-shaped bright pattern.
Noise obscures the L at high strength.
A toy restoration with access to the clean target restores it; a real model does not have that target.
misconception: Removing random noise with the original image in hand reproduces diffusion generation.
correction: This exercise visualizes steps only. Actual generation uses learned denoising without a clean target at inference.
change: Increase noise strength from 0.15 to 0.45 and compare measured error.
metric: Mean absolute pixel error; plus a human quality checklist
lab: Run a denoising illustration and a consent checklist.
output: Step comparison and three task-specific image observations.
reading: Google, Develop a generative AI application
